title: Dengue risk could rise 113% by century-end; Keralam gets an early-warning model - The South First
article_text:
Dengue risk could rise 113% by century-end; Keralam gets an early-warning model
Keralam's dengue warning system analyses climatic conditions along with fluctuations in reported cases to identify periods when the likelihood of transmission may be increasing.
Dileep V Kumar

Published Oct 18, 2026 | 9:30 AM ⚊ Updated Oct 18, 2026 | 9:30 AM

Share

Northeast monsoon brings alternating spells of rain and sunshine that favour the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes.

Make Us Your Preferred Source on Google

Synopsis: With dengue continuing to claim lives in Keralam, a new forecasting system seeks to give health authorities something they have long needed: time to act before an outbreak gathers pace. By combining weather patterns with disease surveillance data, the machine learning-based system can flag districts at risk weeks in advance. Its importance grows as climate change and changing monsoon patterns threaten to make dengue harder to contain.

With dengue continuing to pose a public health challenge in Keralam, a new early-warning system developed by the Institute of Advanced Virology (IAV), Thiruvananthapuram, is set to strengthen the state’s fight against the disease.

The timing is significant, as the Northeast monsoon brings alternating spells of rain and sunshine that favour the breeding of Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit the virus.

The state has reported 12,355 confirmed dengue cases and 44 deaths this year, with 751 cases and one death reported in the first 16 days of October.

Coming against this backdrop is the Dengue Early Warning System (DEWS), the machine learning-based system that can forecast the risk of dengue transmission across districts.

The developers said that the projection is made by analysing weather patterns and reported cases, helping health authorities identify vulnerable areas and step up preventive action before infections surge.

Forecasting dengue risk weeks in advance

The forecasting system developed by the Institute of Advanced Virology

The system, developed by a team led by Dr Abhinand C.S, scientist in the Division of Virus Genomics, Bioinformatics and Statistics at IAV, is designed to identify periods when the risk of dengue transmission is likely to rise.

IAV is an autonomous institution under the Science and Technology Department of the state government. The system is developed and maintained by the IAV as part of its efforts to apply data science and machine learning to public health challenges.

The DEWS’s district-wise forecasts can help officials direct preventive measures to areas that need them most, rather than waiting for a sharp increase in cases to trigger action.

According to officials, DEWS works by combining historical disease surveillance data from the Kerala Health Department and meteorological information from the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Rainfall, temperature, atmospheric humidity and reported dengue cases are among the key variables analysed to assess the likelihood of an outbreak.

The model was developed using daily data covering six years, from March 2020 to February 2026. By examining past outbreaks alongside changes in climatic conditions, it identifies patterns that may signal an increase in transmission risk.

The system generates weekly forecasts for every district in Keralam, including predictions of dengue trends and risk levels several weeks ahead.

The risk is classified into four categories –low, moderate, high and very high– to help identify districts that may require closer monitoring and early intervention.

Also Read: From Keralam to Delhi, women donate more kidneys but receive fewer

Weather and case trends offer early clues

Rainfall, temperature and humidity influence the breeding and survival of Aedes mosquitoes, which transmit dengue. But weather alone cannot explain the course of an outbreak.

DEWS therefore analyses climatic conditions along with fluctuations in reported cases to identify periods when the likelihood of transmission may be increasing.

The system also features an interactive, colour-coded map showing the geographical distribution of predicted dengue cases and highlighting districts according to their forecast risk. The map allows officials to identify potential hotspots and compare the risk across districts.

“A preliminary evaluation using Health Department surveillance data from March to July 2026 found a correlation between the transmission trends predicted by the model and the trends in reported cases,” said an official with the IAV.

The dengue risk map of DEWS for 1 to 7 November

Researchers, however, have stressed that further testing and continuous evaluation are necessary to establish the system’s reliability across districts, different climatic conditions and varying stages of disease transmission.

Forecasts to guide preventive action

The district-level forecasts could help the Health Department intensify mosquito control measures, organise public awareness campaigns, strengthen disease surveillance and prepare healthcare facilities in areas facing a high risk of transmission.

They could also help authorities prioritise the deployment of limited healthcare resources in districts where the threat is greatest. Advance warning of a possible surge would give local health teams more time to act before an outbreak reaches its peak.

DEWS forecast dengue cases from 1 November to 16 January 2027

IAV has emphasised that DEWS is intended to supplement, not replace, existing disease surveillance mechanisms. The institute underscores that its forecasts must be considered alongside the Health Department’s field-level monitoring and expert assessments, with follow-up action essential to translating early warnings into effective prevention.

Initial steps towards such use have already been taken, according to IAV officials.

“The forecasts are intended to support public health planning and should not be treated as official dengue case counts. Data quality, reporting delays and the limitations inherent in predictive models may affect the results,” said the official.

According to the official, while the preliminary findings offer an encouraging indication of the system’s potential, continued validation will be important before its forecasts can be relied upon across different settings.

“The larger aim is to give health authorities an additional tool to recognise emerging risks early and respond before dengue spreads more widely,” the official added.

Also Read: Can a doctor approve your test report without being physically present? NMC clarifies

Dengue cases may rise 113% by century-end

Keralam could face a sharp rise in dengue cases in the coming decades as climate change alters temperature and rainfall patterns, with the risk potentially increasing by up to 113% by the end of the century, a study has warned.

The study, based on 14 years of dengue and climate data from 2006 to 2019, identifies temperature, humidity, monsoon rainfall and the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) as key factors influencing dengue transmission in the state. Projections suggest that dengue incidence could increase by 16%–20% during 2021–2040, with the rise potentially reaching 113% towards the end of the 21st century.

The research was conducted by a team of scientists, including those from the Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology, the ICMR-National Institute of Translational Virology and AIDS Research, and the School of Public Health under the Kerala University of Health Sciences.

Dengue cases in Keralam closely follow the rainfall cycle, with infections beginning to rise in May and peaking during the southwest monsoon, particularly in June and July. Around 60% of the cases reported in the state occur between late May and September.

The study found that warmer pre-monsoon temperatures, moderate relative humidity and increased monsoon rainfall were associated with higher dengue incidence. El Niño conditions in the Pacific Ocean were also linked to local weather patterns favourable to the spread of the disease.

El Niño-like conditions can alter large-scale atmospheric circulation, leaving Keralam warmer and drier during the pre-monsoon period. La Niña-like conditions tend to have the opposite effect. These links could provide forecasts up to three months in advance, offering health authorities a window to prepare for a possible surge in cases.

The researchers analysed monthly dengue figures from the State Surveillance Unit of the Directorate of Health Services. Data from 2020 to 2022 were excluded because the COVID-19 pandemic disrupted surveillance and reporting.

Keralam’s climate makes the state particularly vulnerable to dengue. The combined influence of the southwest and northeast monsoons, high humidity, the Western Ghats and proximity to the Arabian Sea creates favourable conditions for mosquito breeding across much of the year.

The findings underline the need to integrate climate forecasts into dengue surveillance and public health planning. Advance warnings based on temperature, humidity, rainfall and ENSO patterns could help authorities step up mosquito control and other preventive measures before cases begin to climb, the study says.

title: Heavy rain forecast in north Kerala; yellow alert in five districts - Hindusthan Samachar English
article_text:
Thiruvananthapuram, 18 Oct (H.S.): Isolated heavy rain is likely to continue across Kerala on Sunday, with the India Meteorological Department (IMD) warning that showers could intensify in northern districts. A yellow alert has been issued for Kasaragod, Kannur, Wayanad, Kozhikode and Malappuram.
The weather department has also forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning at isolated places. Strong winds reaching speeds of up to 40 kmph are likely alongside the showers, prompting calls for caution in areas experiencing adverse weather.
The rain warning will extend to more districts on Monday. Thrissur and Palakkad will join Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod on the yellow alert list, taking the number of districts under the advisory to seven.
The alerts indicate the possibility of isolated heavy rainfall, with northern Kerala remaining the main area of concern over the two days. Residents have been advised to remain attentive to weather updates as thunderstorms and gusty winds could accompany the rain.
Meanwhile, the IMD has warned fishermen against venturing into the sea along the Kerala, Karnataka and Lakshadweep coasts on Sunday, October 18, citing strong winds and rough weather.
Wind speeds over these coastal waters are expected to range between 35 and 45 kmph, occasionally reaching 55 kmph. The combination of gusty winds and adverse weather is expected to make conditions unsafe for fishing operations.
The advisory covers all three coastal stretches, and fishermen have been asked to refrain from fishing in the affected waters during the warning period.
While the land-based forecast points to isolated spells of heavy rain, the marine warning highlights the risk posed by stronger winds offshore. Coastal communities and fishing crews should take note of the separate sea-weather restrictions.
With rain alerts continuing into Monday, residents in the notified districts should follow subsequent IMD bulletins for any revision to the rainfall forecast and related weather advisories.

title: Maharashtra Weather: ऑक्टोबर हीट पासून दिलासा! राज्यात मुसळधार पाऊस, IMD कडून अलर्ट - Marathi Jagran
article_text:
By: Dnyaneshwar Mathe
Edited By: Dnyaneshwar Mathe
Publish Date: Sun 18 Oct 2026 10:09 AM (IST)
Updated Date: Sun 18 Oct 2026 10:09 AM (IST)
पावसाचा अंदाज

जेएनएन, मुंबई. राज्यात मागील काही दिवसांपासून ऑक्टोबर हीटचा परिणाम वाढला आहे. त्यामुळे राज्यात अनेक जिल्ह्यात उष्णतेचा अलर्टही जारी करण्यात आला होता. मात्र, आता हवामान बदल झाला असून राज्यात पावसाचा अंदाज हवामान विभागाने व्यक्त केला आहे.

10 जिल्ह्यांना पावसाचा यलो अलर्ट

राज्यातील 10 जिल्ह्यांना पावसाचा यलो अलर्ट IMD कडून देण्यात आला आहे. येत्या 24 राज्यात राज्यात पावसाचे वातावरण तयार होण्याची शक्यता आहे. आज रत्नागिरी, सिंधुदुर्ग, कोल्हापूर, कोल्हापूर घाट, सातारा घाट, सांगली, सोलापूर, हिंगोली, नांदेड, लातूर, धाराशीव या जिल्ह्यांत पावसाचा अलर्ट जारी करण्यात आला आहे. तुरळक ठिकाणी ठिजांच्या कडकडाटासह वादळे, हलका ते मध्यम पाऊस आणि सोसाट्याचा वारा (30-40 किमी प्रतितास) येण्याची शक्यता आहे.

उद्या या जिल्ह्यांत पावसाचा अंदाज (Maharashtra Weather Update 19 October)

IMD उद्या म्हणजेच 19 ऑक्टोबर रोजी तुरळक ठिकाणी ठिजांच्या कडकडाटासह वादळे, हलका ते मध्यम पाऊस आणि सोसाट्याचा वारा (30-40 किमी प्रतितास) येण्याची शक्यता आहे. रत्नागिरी, सिंधुदुर्ग, रायगड, पुणे, पुणे घाट, कोल्हापूर, कोल्हापूर घाट, सातारा, सातारा घाट, सांगली, सोलापूर, बीड, लातूर, धाराशीव, गडचिरोली, नागपूर जिल्ह्यात पावसाचा अंदाज वर्तवण्यात आला आहे. या जिल्ह्यांना यलो अलर्ट देण्यात आला आहे.

title: Weather Updates: पावसाचे कमबॅक! अनेक जिल्ह्यात मुसळधार पाऊस; हवामानात मोठे उलटफेर - Dainik Prabhat
article_text:
Weather Updates: पावसाचे कमबॅक! अनेक जिल्ह्यात मुसळधार पाऊस; हवामानात मोठे उलटफेर

Weather Updates: कोल्हापूर, चिपळूण, धुळे जिल्ह्यात मोठ्या खंडानंतर पावसाचा हजेरी

By
Pradnya Pawar
Updated On:
October 18, 2026, 09:08 am

Weather Updates: यंदा राज्यात झालेल्या कमी पावसामुळे दुष्काळाची परिस्थिती ओढावली आहे. याचदरम्यान महाराष्ट्रात ऑक्टोबर हिटमुळे मुंबई, पुणे आणि नाशिकसह संपूर्ण महाराष्ट्रात उन्हाचे चटके जाणवत आहे.

आता नवरात्रीच्या काळात हवामानात मोठे उलटफेर जाणवत आहेत. दक्षिण मध्य महाराष्ट्रासह कोकण आणि मराठवाड्यातील काही जिल्ह्यांत पावसाने हजेरी लावल्याचे चित्र पाहायला मिळाले.  काल कोल्हापूर, चिपळूण, धुळे, सांगलीतील अनेक भागात पावसाच्या सरी बरसल्या. त्यामुळे उकाड्याने हैराण झालेल्या नागरिकांना हवामानात गारवा निर्माण झाल्यामुळे दिलासा मिळाला. तरी दुष्काळाचे संकट दूर होण्यासाठी पावसाची प्रतीक्षा कायम आहे.

आज कुठे-कुठे बरसणार पाऊस? 

कोकण विभागातील पालघर, ठाणे आणि मुंबई येथे आज हवामान प्रामुख्याने कोरडे राहण्याची शक्यता आहे. रायगड आणि रत्नागिरीसह सिंधुदुर्ग जिल्ह्यात हलक्या ते मध्यम सरी पडण्याचा अंदाज आहे.

पश्चिम महाराष्ट्रातील सांगली, कोल्हापूरसह काही भागात गेल्या दोन दिवसांपासून पावसाने हजेरी लावली. आज पुणे, सातारा आणि घाटमाथ्याच्या परिसरात हलक्या ते मध्यम सरी पडण्याची शक्यता आहे. कोल्हापूर, सातारा, सांगली आणि सोलापूर जिल्ह्यांमध्ये काही भागांसाठी येलो अलर्ट देण्यात आला आहे. पुढील दोन ते तीन दिवस काही भागांमध्ये पावसाचे वातावरण कायम राहू शकते.

मराठवाड्यात छत्रपती संभाजीनगर आणि जालना येथे हवामान प्रामुख्याने कोरडे राहण्याची शक्यता आहे. परभणी आणि बीड जिल्ह्यांत हलक्या सरींचा अंदाज आहे. तर हिंगोली, नांदेड, लातूर आणि धाराशिव जिल्ह्यांत येलो अलर्ट देण्यात आला आहे. विदर्भातील बहुतांश जिल्ह्यांमध्ये हवामान कोरडे, ढगाळ आणि काही ठिकाणी दमट राहण्याची शक्यता आहे.

सांगलीत दमदार पाऊस

दरम्यान, चिपळूण, धुळे जिल्ह्यात मोठ्या खंडानंतर पावसाने हजेरी लावली. सांगलीतील तासगाव तालुक्याचा नुकताच दुष्काळी यादीत समावेश झाला आहे. काल तासगाव तालुक्यातील काही गावांमध्ये भर दुपारी झालेल्या मुसळधार पावसामुळे या भागातील रब्बी पेरणी केलेल्या पिकांना काही प्रमाणात दिलासा मिळण्याची शक्यता आहे.

title: 'Bangalore Is Bangaloring': City Drenched Again With Heavy Rain; Check Bengaluru Weather Today June 13 - Goodreturns
article_text:
Bengaluru weather turned stormy as heavy rainfall lashed large parts of the city late on June 12, with areas including Agara, Marathahalli, koramangla, Hebbal, and neighbourhoods across both north and south Bengaluru.
On Saturday morning, many residents woke up to waterlogged streets and overflowing drains. Continuing its trend from last night, Bengaluru weather today is expected to be no different. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) and Karnataka State Natural Disaster Monitoring Centre (KSNDMC) have issued warnings across the state as the southwest monsoon has covered the whole of Karnataka.
The city is experiencing cool & wet conditions this morning as current temperature stands at 20°C with humidity at a high 94%, and the day is expected to peak at 28°C. Conditions remain cloudy with thunder and lightning likely through the day, with light to moderate rain and heavy rain at isolated places across Bengaluru. Waterlogging, traffic issues can be seen in low-lying areas.
IMD's sub-division-wise warnings issued on June 12 show that Coastal Karnataka weather is under a heavy rain and strong surface winds alert today, while North Interior Karnataka weather is facing heavy rain along with thunderstorms, lightning, and squall conditions.
South Interior Karnataka, including Bengaluru, is also under a heavy rain and strong surface winds warning issued by IMD
Coastal Karnataka saw the most intense rainfall in the past 24 hours, with Hassan's Channarayapatna Santeshivara recording the highest at 76.5 mm, followed by Udupi Karkala Kuchluru at 68 mm and Udupi Kundapur Madanakki at 65.5 mm.
In Bengaluru's extended region, Karahalli in Devanahalli taluk recorded 91 mm and Doddurukarapanahalli in Bangarpet taluk recorded 90 mm on the evening of June 12.
The river Doni at Talikot in Vijayapura district is currently flowing above the warning level as of June 12, 2026. Residents in low-lying areas near rivers across Karnataka are advised to remain alert.
Heavy rain and strong winds will continue across coastal and interior Karnataka through June 15. Rainfall activity is expected to reduce from June 16 onwards, with no major warnings currently in place for June 16-18 across all three sub-divisions.

title: Odisha Weather Alert: Depression Weakens, Thunderstorm Warning Issued - Pragativadi
article_text:
A persistent weather depression centred over northeast Madhya Pradesh and adjoining north Chhattisgarh continues its north-northwestward journey, bringing heavy precipitation across central and eastern India.

While the system is expected to lose intensity over the next 12 to 24 hours, meteorologists have sounded a high alert for Odisha, where intense rainfall and thunderstorms threaten multiple districts.

Depression Trajectory & Weakening Forecast

Moving at a speed of 13 km/h over the past six hours, the depression was centred near latitude 23.8°N and longitude 81.6°E.

The system lies approximately:

70 km south-southwest of Sidhi (MP)

90 km south-southeast of Rewa (MP)

120 km southeast of Satna (MP)

180 km south of Prayagraj (UP)

250 km south-southeast of Fatehpur (UP)

According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the depression will maintain its current intensity as it moves across northeast Madhya Pradesh toward southeast Uttar Pradesh. It is projected to gradually weaken into a well-marked low-pressure area during the subsequent 12 hours. Radar stations at Raipur and Lucknow are continuously monitoring the system’s trajectory.

Torrential Downpours Inundate Odisha

Even as the atmospheric depression shifts away, its trailing arm has triggered widespread heavy to very heavy rainfall across eastern India. Odisha recorded intense precipitation at 19 key locations across nine districts during the 24-hour period ending Saturday morning.

Location District Recorded Rainfall Rainfall Category Nawana Mayurbhanj 126 mm Very Heavy Rainfall Raighar Nabarangpur 107 mm Heavy Rainfall Khaira Baleshwar 101 mm Heavy Rainfall

Thunderstorm & Safety Warnings Issued

The regional weather office has extended a thunderstorm warning valid until Sunday morning, cautioning residents against short-duration, high-intensity lightning and gusty winds.

Alerted Districts: Kendujhar, Mayurbhanj, Baleshwar, Bhadrak, Jajpur, Sundaragada, Jagatsinghpur, Kendrapada, Khordha, Kataka, Puri, Nayagada, Anugola, Dhenkanal, and Debagada.

Disaster management authorities have advised residents in the designated districts to avoid sheltering under trees or near untethered structures during lightning strikes and to monitor official advisories closely.

title: Gujarat among states on alert as MHA warns of heavy rain from inland depression - DD News
article_text:
The Union Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has directed the Gujarat government and other concerned states to closely monitor the evolving weather situation after a depression over north interior Odisha and adjoining south Jharkhand intensified the risk of widespread heavy rainfall across central and western India.

In an advisory issued by the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response (ICR-ER) at 1 a.m. on Monday, the MHA said the depression, which had moved northwestwards at about 13 kmph over the previous six hours, was centred over north interior Odisha and adjoining south Jharkhand at 11:30 p.m. on Sunday.

It was located near latitude 22.1 degrees N and longitude 86.0 degrees E, around 80 km west-northwest of Baripada, 70 km northeast of Keonjhargarh, 80 km south-southwest of Jamshedpur and 180 km east-southeast of Rourkela.

The system is expected to continue moving nearly west-northwestwards across north Odisha, adjoining south Jharkhand and north Chhattisgarh during the next 24 hours.

For Gujarat, the advisory forecasts light to moderate rainfall at most places, with heavy to very heavy rainfall expected at a few places and isolated extremely heavy rainfall on July 6 and 7.

Heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places on July 8, followed by heavy rainfall at isolated places on July 9.

Saurashtra and Kutch are also expected to receive light to moderate rainfall at most places, with isolated heavy to very heavy rainfall on July 6 and 7 and heavy rainfall on July 8 and 9.

The advisory is in line with the latest warnings issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD), which has placed the Gujarat region under an extremely heavy rainfall warning for July 6 and 7, while Saurashtra and Kutch remain under very heavy rainfall warnings during the same period.

IMD has also forecast thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and squally winds over parts of Gujarat on Monday.

The IMD’s Ahmedabad Meteorological Centre has forecast widespread rain and thundershowers across much of the state, with rainfall expected at many places in North Gujarat and Saurashtra and at most places in South Gujarat over the next two days.

Apart from Gujarat, the MHA advisory warns of heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, East Rajasthan and Madhya Maharashtra, while heavy rainfall is also expected over Jharkhand, Bihar, Gangetic West Bengal, Marathwada, Vidarbha and parts of Uttar Pradesh.

The advisory further states that squally winds reaching 35-45 kmph, gusting to 55 kmph, are likely over north interior Odisha, adjoining south Jharkhand and north Chhattisgarh until the morning of July 7.

Over the northwest Bay of Bengal and along the Odisha, West Bengal and north Andhra Pradesh coasts, winds of up to 55 kmph, gusting to 65 kmph, are expected before gradually weakening.

Sea conditions are forecast to remain rough over the northwest Bay of Bengal and along the Odisha, West Bengal and north Andhra Pradesh coasts until July 7, while conditions over the central and northeast Bay of Bengal are expected to improve after Monday morning.

Fishermen have been advised not to venture into the northwest Bay of Bengal and along the Odisha, West Bengal and north Andhra Pradesh coasts until July 7.

They have also been warned against venturing into the central and northeast Bay of Bengal during the next 24 hours.

The MHA said the expected impacts include uprooting of small trees, damage to plantations and standing crops, minor damage to vulnerable structures and kutcha houses, waterlogging in low-lying areas, localised flooding, landslides, disruption to road and rail transport, reduced visibility and possible disruption to helicopter services.

The advisory said: “People are advised to keep a watch on the weather for worsening conditions and be ready to move to safer places accordingly. Take safe shelters; do not take shelter under trees, as there could be lightning.”

The MHA has asked all concerned state governments to maintain close monitoring of the situation, ensure district authorities remain alert and take all necessary precautionary measures.

States have also been requested to keep the ministry informed of any significant developments through the Integrated Control Room for Emergency Response.

-IANS

title: દેશના 15 રાજ્યમાં ભારે વરસાદનું એલર્ટ, જાણો ગુજરાતમાં કેવું રહેશે હવામાન - Mumbai Samachar
article_text:
Mumbai Samachar
/
gujarat
/
imd-weather-alert-heavy-rain-15-states-monsoon-withdrawl-gujarat
દેશના 15 રાજ્યમાં ભારે વરસાદનું એલર્ટ, જાણો ગુજરાતમાં કેવું રહેશે હવામાન
2026-09-25 08:35:00
Author: Mayur Patel



અમદાવાદ/નવી દિલ્હીઃ દેશના ઘણા ભાગોમાંથી વરસાદની વિદાયની શરૂઆત થઈ ચુકી છે. હાલ વરસાદનો અંતિમ તબક્કો ચાલી રહ્યો છે. અંતિમ રાઉન્ડમાં પણ કેટલાક રાજ્યોમાં વરસાદ ધબધબાટી બોલાવી રહ્યો છે. ભારતીય હવામાન વિભાગની આગાહી મુજબ, આજે એટલે કે 25 સપ્ટેમ્બરે દેશના 15 રાજ્યોમાં હળવાથી ભારે વરસાદ થઈ શકે છે. આ દરમિયાન વાવાઝોડા સાથે વીજળી પડવાની પણ શક્યતા છે. તેમજ 40 થી 85 કિલોમીટર પ્રતિ કલાકની ઝડપે તેજ પવન ફૂંકાઈ શકે છે. આ ઉપરાંત IMD એ ઓડિશા, છત્તીસગઢ, પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ, ઝારખંડ અને આંધ્રપ્રદેશના તટીય વિસ્તારોમાં આગામી 24 કલાકમાં અચાનક પૂર આવવાની ચેતવણી આપી છે. હવામાન વિભાગે ગુજરાતમાં કેટલાક સ્થળોએ વરસાદી ઝાપટાં પડવાની આગાહી કરી છે.

ગુજરાતમાં કેવું રહેશે હવામાન

ગુજરાતમાં ચોમાસાની વિદાયની પ્રક્રિયા આગળ વધી રહી છે અને હવે રાજ્યમાં વરસાદનું જોર ધીમે ધીમે ઘટવાની શક્યતા છે. જેના કારણે ગુજરાતના મોટાભાગના વિસ્તારોમાં ગરમીનું પ્રમાણ વધી રહ્યું છે. હવામાન વિભાગે આગામી 30 સપ્ટેમ્બર સુધી ગુજરાતમાં વરસાદની ગતિવિધિમાં ઘટાડો થવાની આગાહી કરી છે. જોકે, દક્ષિણ ગુજરાત સહિત કેટલાક વિસ્તારોમાં હળવાથી સામાન્ય વરસાદ ચાલુ રહી શકે છે.  સૌરાષ્ટ્ર, કચ્છ અને ઉત્તર ગુજરાતના કેટલાક વિસ્તારોમાં આજે વરસાદની શક્યતા નથી. જ્યારે રાજ્યના બાકીના વિસ્તારોમાં હળવાથી સામાન્ય વરસાદ પડી શકે છે. આગામી દિવસોમાં વરસાદનું પ્રમાણ વધુ ઘટવાની શક્યતા છે અને ચોમાસાની વિદાયની પ્રક્રિયા આગળ વધશે. રાજ્યમાં છેલ્લા 24 કલાકમાં એક પણ તાલુકામાં વરસાદ પડ્યો ન હોવાનું સ્ટેટ ઈમરજન્સી ઓપરેશન સેન્ટર, ગાંધીનગરના રિપોર્ટમાં જણાવાયું છે.

અંબાલાલે શું કરી છે આગાહી

ચોમાસાની વિદાય વચ્ચે ગુજરાતમાં ગરમી વધવાની શક્યતા પણ છે. અંબાલાલ પટેલની આગાહી મુજબ, 25 સપ્ટેમ્બર સુધીમાં ગરમીમાં વધારો થઈ શકે છે અને કેટલાક વિસ્તારોમાં તાપમાન 40 ડિગ્રી સેલ્સિયસ સુધી પહોંચી શકે છે. જોકે, 26થી 28 સપ્ટેમ્બર દરમિયાન ગરમીમાં થોડો ઘટાડો થવાની શક્યતા છે. ત્યારબાદ 29 અને 30 સપ્ટેમ્બરે ફરી ગરમી વધવાની શક્યતા વ્યક્ત કરવામાં આવી છે. 

હવામાન વિભાગ અનુસાર, ઓડિશા, છત્તીસગઢ, આંધ્ર પ્રદેશ જેવા રાજ્યોમાં પણ મુશળધાર વરસાદ પડશે. જમ્મુ-કાશ્મીર, લદ્દાખ, હિમાચલ પ્રદેશ, ઉત્તરાખંડમાં કાલે એટલે કે 25 સપ્ટેમ્બરે ભારે વરસાદ, વીજળીના કડાકા અને આંધી-તોફાનની ચેતવણી છે. પૂર્વી ઉત્તર પ્રદેશમાં પણ ભારે વરસાદનું એલર્ટ જાહેર કરવામાં આવ્યું છે. ઉત્તર-પશ્ચિમના કેટલાક વિસ્તારોમાં પણ કાલે વીજળીના કડાકા સાથે વરસાદ થવાની સંભાવના છે.   પશ્ચિમ મધ્ય પ્રદેશ, પૂર્વ મધ્ય પ્રદેશ, છત્તીસગઢ, વિદર્ભમાં કેટલાક વિસ્તારોમાં અતિ ભારે વરસાદ પણ થઈ શકે છે. આ દરમિયાન છત્તીસગઢમાં તેજ પવન પણ ફૂંકાશે, જેની ઝડપ 70 કિલોમીટર પ્રતિ કલાક સુધી પહોંચી શકે છે. ડમાન અને નિકોબાર દ્વીપસમૂહ, બિહાર, ગંગાના મેદાની વિસ્તારો ધરાવતા પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ, ઝારખંડ, ઓડિશા, ઉપ-હિમાલયી પશ્ચિમ બંગાળ, સિક્કિમમાં ભારે વરસાદ પડશે.

હવામાન વિભાગના જણાવ્યા અનુસાર, બંગાળની ખાડીમાં સર્જાયેલા ડીપ ડિપ્રેશનની અસરથી પશ્ચિમ-મધ્ય અને તેને અડીને આવેલી ઉત્તર-પશ્ચિમ બંગાળની ખાડીમાં તેજ પવન ફૂંકાઈ રહ્યો છે. દક્ષિણ ઓડિશા, ઉત્તર આંધ્રપ્રદેશ અને યાનમના દરિયાકાંઠા પાસે પવનની ગતિ 55-65 કિલોમીટર પ્રતિ કલાક છે અને ઝાપટાં સાથે તે 75 કિલોમીટર પ્રતિ કલાક સુધી પહોંચી શકે છે. આ સાથે જ ચોમાસાની વિદાય શરૂ થઈ ગઈ છે. નૈઋત્યના ચોમાસાની રેખા ગુરદાસપુર, ચંદીગઢ, મુઝફ્ફરનગર, અલીગઢ, ધોલપુર, ઉદયપુર અને નલિયા પરથી પસાર થઈ રહી છે.

title: Weather Update Today: सावधान! आज 23 राज्यों में आंधी-तूफान संग होगी बारिश, बिहार-यूपी से लेकर दिल्ली तक बिगड़ेगा मौसम, यहां पढ़ें IMD का वेदर अपडेट - गुड न्यूज़ टुडे
article_text:
मॉनसून की विदाई के बाद भी देश के कई राज्यों में मौसम का मिजाज बिगड़ने वाला है. भारतीय मौसम विभाग (IMD) के पूर्वानुमान के मुताबिक 18 अक्टूबर, दिन रविवार को उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार, दिल्ली, पंजाब, हरियाणा समेत देश के 23 राज्यों में बारिश और तेज आंधी की चेतावनी जारी की गई है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 70 से 75 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. कई राज्यों में आकाशीय बिजली गिरने और ओलावृष्टि की आशंका जताई गई है.
पश्चिम बंगाल, उत्तराखंड, ओडिशा, तेलंगाना और आंध्र प्रदेश के कुछ हिस्सों में मौसम का असर अधिक देखने को मिल सकता है. इसके अलावा हिमाचल प्रदेश, उत्तराखंड और जम्मू-कश्मीर के ऊंचाई वाले इलाकों में बर्फबारी की संभावना से ठंड बढ़ सकती है. खराब मौसम के कारण किसानों की फसलों को नुकसान पहुंचने की आशंका है. मौसम में बदलाव के चलते कुछ इलाकों में तापमान 2 से 3 डिग्री सेल्सियस तक गिर सकता है. मौसम में इस बदलाव के पीछे बंगाल की खाड़ी में बन रहा निम्न दबाव का क्षेत्र और उत्तर-पश्चिमी उत्तर प्रदेश सहित आसपास के इलाकों में सक्रिय चक्रवाती परिसंचरण जैसे मौसमी कारक बताए गए हैं. ऐसे में लोगों को खराब मौसम के दौरान सतर्क रहने, खुले स्थानों और पेड़ों के नीचे खड़े होने से बचने तथा मौसम विभाग की चेतावनियों पर ध्यान देने की सलाह मौसम विभाग की तरफ से दी गई है.
आज इन राज्यों में बारिश और आंधी का अलर्ट
मौसम विभाग के पूर्वानुमान के अनुसार, 18 अक्टूबर को उत्तर प्रदेश, बिहार, दिल्ली, हरियाणा, राजस्थान, हिमाचल प्रदेश, उत्तराखंड, पंजाब, जम्मू-कश्मीर, झारखंड, ओडिशा, पश्चिम बंगाल, छत्तीसगढ़, मध्य प्रदेश, गुजरात, महाराष्ट्र, तेलंगाना, कर्नाटक, आंध्र प्रदेश, तमिलनाडु, असम, त्रिपुरा और नागालैंड समेत कई राज्यों में बारिश और तेज हवाओं का असर देखने को मिल सकता है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 70 से 75 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंचने की आशंका है. उत्तर भारत और पूर्वी भारत के कई जिलों में बिजली गिरने और वज्रपात का खतरा बना रह सकता है. कुछ राज्यों में ओलावृष्टि की भी संभावना है.
दिल्ली में आज कैसा रहेगा मौसम?
दिल्ली में 18 अक्टूबर 2026 को बारिश और आंधी की चेतावनी जारी की गई है. इस दौरान 40 से 45 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से तेज हवाएं चल सकती हैं. रविवार को राजधानी में अधिकतम तापमान करीब 31 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 18 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है. मौसम में बदलाव से लोगों को गर्मी से कुछ राहत मिल सकती है.
उत्तर प्रदेश में कई जिलों में बारिश का अलर्ट
उत्तर प्रदेश में कई जिलों में रविवार को बारिश का अलर्ट है. यूपी के मेरठ, गौतमबुद्ध नगर, मुरादाबाद, मुजफ्फरनगर, शामली, रामपुर, अलीगढ़, अमरोहा, आगरा, मथुरा, हापुड़, लखीमपुर खीरी, हाथरस, सहारनपुर, इटावा, झांसी, हरदोई, उन्नाव, ललितपुर, देवरिया, हमीरपुर, सुल्तानपुर, आजमगढ़, अयोध्या, प्रयागराज, मैनपुरी और गोरखपुर समेत कई जिलों में बारिश और आंधी का येलो अलर्ट है. राजधानी लखनऊ में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने का अनुमान है. बारिश और तेज हवाओं के कारण कुछ इलाकों में तापमान में गिरावट आ सकती है.
बिहार में तेज हवा के साथ भारी बारिश की आशंका
मौसम विभाग ने बिहार के कई जिलों रविवार को तेज हवा के साथ भारी बारिश की आशंका जताई है. बिहार की राजधानी पटना, सिवान, सारण, गोपालगंज, पूर्वी चंपारण, गया, जहानाबाद, भोजपुर, बक्सर, वैशाली, समस्तीपुर, दरभंगा, मधुबनी, सुपौल, सहरसा, पूर्णिया, किशनगंज, अररिया, कटिहार, भागलपुर, मुंगेर और बेगूसराय में बारिश और आंधी की चेतावनी है. इन इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 50 से 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. पटना में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 21 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
झारखंड में आज और कल बिगड़ सकता है मौसम
मौसम विभाग के मुताबिक झारखंड में 18 और 19 अक्टूबर को मौसम बिगड़ सकता है.  झारखंड के राजधानी रांची, बोकारो, रामगढ़, खूंटी, जमशेदपुर, चतरा, देवघर, पश्चिमी सिंहभूम, दुमका, पलामू, हजारीबाग, धनबाद, गिरिडीह, लातेहार और सिमडेगा समेत कई जिलों में तेज बारिश और आंधी की आशंका है. इस दौरान हवा की रफ्तार 60 से 65 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. रांची में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान 29 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 19 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
उत्तराखंड में बारिश और बर्फबारी की संभावना
उत्तराखंड के ऋषिकेश, हरिद्वार, नैनीताल, पिथौरागढ़, पौड़ी गढ़वाल, टिहरी गढ़वाल, उत्तरकाशी, बागेश्वर और चमोली में रविवार को बारिश और तेज हवाओं की चेतावनी दी गई है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. ऊंचाई वाले क्षेत्रों में बर्फबारी की संभावना से ठंड बढ़ सकती है. देहरादून में अधिकतम तापमान रविवार को करीब 27 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 14 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
हिमाचल प्रदेश में तेज हवाओं के साथ बारिश का अलर्ट
मौसम विभाग ने रविवार को हिमाचल प्रदेश के कई जिलों में तेज हवाओं के साथ बारिश का अलर्ट जारी किया है. हिमाचल प्रदेश के ऊना, कांगड़ा, चंबा, हमीरपुर, बिलासपुर, मंडी, सोलन और किन्नौर में बारिश और तेज हवाओं की चेतावनी जारी की गई है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 50 से 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. पहाड़ी क्षेत्रों में बर्फबारी होने से आवागमन प्रभावित होने की आशंका भी बनी रह सकती है. मनाली में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान करीब 6 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान माइनस 4 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
जम्मू-कश्मीर में बारिश और तेज आंधी की संभावना
जम्मू-कश्मीर के अनंतनाग, जम्मू, पुंछ, किश्तवाड़, बारामूला, गांदरबल, उधमपुर, रामबन, शोपियां और बांदीपोरा समेत कई इलाकों में बारिश और तेज हवाओं का अलर्ट बताया गया है. कुछ स्थानों पर हवा की रफ्तार 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. श्रीनगर में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान करीब 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 12 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
पश्चिम बंगाल में 70 किमी प्रति घंटे की रफ्तार से चल सकती हैं हवाएं
पश्चिम बंगाल के कोलकाता, हावड़ा, जलपाईगुड़ी, बांकुड़ा, कालिम्पोंग, अलीपुरद्वार, झाड़ग्राम, पश्चिम मेदिनीपुर, दार्जिलिंग, कूचबिहार, दुर्गापुर और बीरभूम में रविवार को तेज बारिश और आंधी की आशंका है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 70 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. कोलकाता में रविवार अधिकतम तापमान 34 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 24 डिग्री सेल्सियस के आसपास रहने का अनुमान है.
पंजाब में बारिश और तेज हवाओं से बढ़ेगी परेशानी
पंजाब के होशियारपुर, कपूरथला, चंडीगढ़, संगरूर, लुधियाना, अमृतसर, बठिंडा, फरीदकोट और बरनाला में बारिश और आंधी की चेतावनी दी गई है. इस दौरान हवा की रफ्तार 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. किसानों को खेतों में खड़ी फसलों और खुले में रखी उपज की सुरक्षा पर ध्यान देने की जरूरत है.
राजस्थान में कई जिलों में मध्यम से भारी बारिश के आसार
राजस्थान के बारां, चूरू, सवाई माधोपुर, कोटा, जयपुर, उदयपुर, दौसा, बाड़मेर, भीलवाड़ा, भरतपुर, जैसलमेर, अलवर और जालौर में मध्यम से भारी बारिश की संभावना जताई गई है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 50 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. जयपुर में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान करीब 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 21 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
मध्य प्रदेश में तेज आंधी और बारिश का अलर्ट
मध्य प्रदेश के दमोह, विदिशा, कटनी, नर्मदापुरम, बालाघाट, बैतूल, मंडला, भोपाल, खंडवा, नरसिंहपुर, देवास, हरदा और सागर में बारिश और तेज आंधी की चेतावनी दी गई है. हवा की रफ्तार 55 से 60 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है. भोपाल में रविवार को अधिकतम तापमान 32 डिग्री सेल्सियस और न्यूनतम तापमान 22 डिग्री सेल्सियस रहने का अनुमान है.
छत्तीसगढ़ में बारिश और तेज हवाओं की चेतावनी
छत्तीसगढ़ के बीजापुर, नारायणपुर, सूरजपुर, बिलासपुर, रायपुर, धमतरी, जांजगीर, कोरबा और महासमुंद में भारी बारिश और आंधी की संभावना जताई गई है. इस दौरान हवा की रफ्तार 55 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है.
ओडिशा में तेज हवाओं के साथ भारी बारिश का खतरा
ओडिशा के जाजपुर, गंजाम, गजपति, बलांगीर, नुआपाड़ा, भुवनेश्वर, सुंदरगढ़, भद्रक, कटक, बालासोर, मयूरभंज, पुरी और कंधमाल में भारी बारिश की चेतावनी दी गई है. कुछ इलाकों में हवा की रफ्तार 65 किलोमीटर प्रति घंटे तक पहुंच सकती है.

title: IMD issues red alert for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall in coastal Andhra Pradesh - News On AIR
article_text:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for very heavy to extremely heavy rainfall over Coastal Andhra Pradesh for the day. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Kerala, Mahe, South Interior Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal till tomorrow.

The Met Department said that thunderstorms and lightning conditions will continue over Konkan, Goa, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, and Lakshadweep till tomorrow. Similar weather conditions are also expected over East Rajasthan, East Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the day.

Weather Update: MP में मालवा निमाड़ में बारिश, उत्तर और दक्षिण भारत में भी बारिश, खतरनाक चक्रवात चंपी चीन से टकराएगा

दिनेश सोलंकी की खास रिपोर्ट 

मध्य प्रदेश का मौसम अगले 7 दिन तक बादलों की गिरफ्त में रहने की संभावना है। यहां अरब सागर से बादलों की लहर गुजरात से मध्य प्रदेश होते हुए यूपी, बिहार की तरफ जा रही है। जिसके चलते गुजरात के कुछ हिस्सों में और मध्य प्रदेश के मालवा निमाड़ तथा मध्य क्षेत्र में बादलों की अधिकता से बारिश की संभावना बन रही है। भारी बारिश की संभावना नहीं है, लेकिन रिमझिम से लेकर सामान्य बारिश कहीं-कहीं हो सकती है, ऐसा माहौल पूरे सप्ताह रहेगा। इसी के चलते न्यूनतम तापमान में 2 डिग्री और अधिकतम तापमान में एक डिग्री कम का असर देखा जा रहा है जो अगले 24 घंटे में और भी कम हो सकता है। 36 डिग्री तक जा पहुंचे ग्वालियर में भी अधिकतम तापमान में चार डिग्री की कमी आई है।

उत्तर भारत में आज भी जम्मू कश्मीर और लद्दाख में बर्फबारी की संभावना है, वहीं हिमाचल प्रदेश के पहाड़ी क्षेत्र में भी हल्की बर्फबारी हो सकती है। राजस्थान के उत्तर पश्चिम भाग में सुबह से कोहरा छाया रहेगा इसके अलावा हरियाणा के दक्षिण दिल्ली और यूपी के उत्तरी भाग में भी आज घना कोर चने की संभावना रहेगी राजस्थान के दक्षिण- पूर्वी भाग में कहीं-कहीं बारिश की
